assumptions: associativity tested on all evaluable triples in [0,16)^3 and [0,64)^3 (triples whose intermediate value is >= 64 are skipped and counted)
properties on finite windows only; an operation is called associative here if no violation is found on the evaluated triples
meta.falsification: H-C07-1: an associative non-trivial operation other than XOR and nim-product. H-C07-2: a commutative operation not closed on [0,2), [0,4) or [0,16).
meta.hypothesis: H-C07-1 (bold): apart from trivial operations, the only associative operations of the family are Conway's nim-sum and nim-product. H-C07-2 (bold): every commutative operation of the family is closed on the 'Fermat' segments [0, 2^(2^m)), m = 0, 1, 2, like the nimbers.
meta.methodology: Compute the 64 x 64 table of every spec (vectorised mex, cross-checked against a plain-set implementation); group identical tables; record commutativity, closure on [0, 2^j), associativity violations, identities, XOR-distributivity and the Latin property on [0, 16).
meta.question: Which operations f(a,b) = mex V(a,b) of the family (L, R, D) (options f(a',b), f(a,b') and XOR combinations of f(a',b), f(a,b'), f(a',b')) are associative, commutative, closed on initial segments, have identities, distribute over XOR?
meta.title: Census of mex-defined binary operations: closure, associativity, identities, distributivity

summary: 512 specs -> 134 distinct operations on [0,64)^2; commutative: 34; associative on the tested windows: 11
